# Proposal: Fractional AI Governance Advisor

**Prepared for:** Dana Whitfield, General Counsel, Tamarack Instruments
**Program:** Fractional AI Governance Advisor, AI Governance Academy
**Basis:** Client Profile Block v1.0 and discovery call notes of 6 October 2026

## 1. Situation Summary

Dana Whitfield, this proposal responds to the objective you stated: "I want governance in place before visual inspection goes into production in Q2 2027."

The Profile Block records the following for Tamarack Instruments:

- **Business:** The Client designs and manufactures laboratory measurement instruments. It is headquartered in the Netherlands and operates in the Netherlands, Germany and the United States.
- **AI use:**
  - Deployed: a customer service chatbot on the support portal.
  - Piloting: AI visual inspection on the German production line.
  - Planned: AI sales forecasting next year.
- **Maturity and drivers:** AI maturity is recorded as Piloting. The regulatory drivers are the EU AI Act and GDPR.
- **Certification target:** ISO/IEC 42001, with work to start next year. The start date is not fixed.
- **Risk event:** An internal audit finding in June 2026 recorded no inventory of AI systems.
- **Incumbent frameworks:** ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS, ISO 9001 quality management system and an internal audit function. The program will confirm at intake which documented processes, controls and records exist under these frameworks that AI governance work could build on.
- **Constraints:**
  - Budget is approved up to US$80,000 this fiscal year.
  - Customer data must stay in the EU.
  - The German works council is consulted before anything touches production staff.

The Client has not completed a prior Academy program, so there are no carried-forward open items.

## 2. The Case for Continuous Fractional Advisory at the Piloting Stage

At the Piloting stage, governance decisions are made while systems are still changing. The Profile Block shows one system deployed, one in pilot with a stated production objective in Q2 2027 and one planned for next year.

A single assessment would describe one moment in that sequence. A twelve-month fractional engagement stays alongside the Client as each system moves through its stage. It also keeps the ISO/IEC 42001 readiness work connected to the systems the Client is actually operating.

The program is built on three principles:

- **Slow AI:** decisions are paced to the evidence available.
- **Informed Intent:** each AI use has a documented purpose and owner.
- **Final Liability rests with the Human:** accountability for AI outcomes stays with named people at the Client.

The program uses two open frameworks:

- GRC Workbook (https://github.com/rolldabones/grc-workbook)
- Slow AI Kitchen (https://github.com/rolldabones/slow-ai-kitchen)

Where executive or board reporting is required, the program references AI Governance for Boards (https://github.com/rolldabones/ai-governance-for-boards).

## 3. The Annual Arc

The engagement start date is Unknown and is to be confirmed at intake. The quarters below are engagement quarters. They are sequenced so that governance for visual inspection is the focus before the stated Q2 2027 production objective. ISO/IEC 42001 readiness work intensifies once its start date is set.

The ISO/IEC 42001 start date and any external audit date are currently Unknown and are flagged for intake. If the engagement starts close to Q2 2027, Quarters 1 and 2 will need to be compressed. That compression will be agreed at intake.

**Quarter 1: Stabilize**
- Establish an AI system inventory in response to the June 2026 internal audit finding.
- Define governance roles and decision rights using the GRC Workbook.
- Prepare questions on EU AI Act classification for each inventoried system, for verification by external counsel.
- Begin the pre-production governance file for AI visual inspection.

**Quarter 2: Deepen**
- Complete the governance file for visual inspection ahead of the stated Q2 2027 objective. This covers risk assessment, human oversight design, monitoring and change control.
- Prepare briefing material the Client may use in its works council consultation. The consultation itself remains with the Client.
- Review the customer service chatbot against the EU data residency constraint and GDPR questions, which are flagged for counsel verification.

**Quarter 3: Assure**
- Conduct an ISO/IEC 42001 readiness gap review, timed to the confirmed start date.
- Design evidence collection for the AI management system.
- Agree with the Client how the internal audit function can test AI controls.
- Prepare a governance intake for the planned sales forecasting use case.

**Quarter 4: Evolve**
- Prepare a management review readiness pack.
- Report readiness status against ISO/IEC 42001 in readiness language only. The program does not promise any certification or audit outcome.
- Update the governance roadmap for the following year.
- Prepare the Month 11 renewal or handover options.

## 4. Cadence and Access Model

The engagement runs on four standing commitments:

- **Monthly executive advisory session:** decisions, risks and regulatory developments flagged for counsel verification.
- **Monthly working session with the governance team:** artifact development and review.
- **Asynchronous availability:** for defined question categories, with response windows agreed at intake.
- **Quarterly governance review:** progress against the annual plan and audit preparation status.

The Profile Block lists the General Counsel, CISO, Head of Quality, Head of Data, German plant manager and two internal auditors as audience roles. Attendance for each session is to be confirmed at intake.

## 5. Scope and Out of Scope

**In scope:**
- Governance evolution
- Implementation guidance
- Audit preparation
- AI strategy
- Executive decision support

**Out of scope:**
- Legal advice
- Certification body functions
- Staff augmentation
- Incident command

The advisor is not counsel of record. Legal questions, including EU AI Act classification and GDPR interpretation, route to external counsel. Regulatory developments raised in the program are flagged for verification and are not settled advice.

## 6. Price

The engagement runs for 12 months, renewable, at US$10,000 per month.

The Profile Block records budget approved up to US$80,000 this fiscal year. Twelve months at US$10,000 per month exceeds that figure. The Client's fiscal year boundaries and the funding route for months beyond the current approval are Unknown and are to be confirmed before contracting. The price and duration are fixed program terms.
